persona.who: 29, chartered accountant in Indore, married 1 year, lives with in-laws who expect her to give up the practice after a baby. Husband avoids the topic.
persona.note: my mother in law keeps saying once the baby comes you will anyway leave all this CA work. I built my practice from zero. my husband just changes the subject. I feel like I am slowly being erased

understanding.bridge: The life she is being erased from is the one she built from zero, and the texts say what is yours cannot be taken by the picture others hold of you.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being erased to standing in the one thing they cannot take: the practice you built from nothing.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being erased, and the anger of it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman who built a CA practice from zero is being told by her mother-in-law she will leave it after the baby, while her husband changes the subject, and she feels herself being erased.
understanding.mirror: You built this practice from nothing, and they speak as if it belongs to someone else.
understanding.insight: They speak of a life you have not yet lived, as if it were already decided, and the only person who can correct it is silent.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Tension with my in-laws. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing, gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit their picture.
queries.story: A woman of standing and learning, dismissed by her husband's family and abandoned by her own, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that it is better to follow your own path, even if you stumble on it, than to take on someone else's life and do it perfectly. The idea is that a borrowed life brings constant fear because it is not yours to own. Your own path, with all its flaws, is the only one that can truly be yours. The anger you feel right now comes from watching someone else try to write your ending while you stand silent.
verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi tells Yudhishthira that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act. She warns him that a person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity. She argues that effort still matters, that fate rewards no one who waits.
verse.for_you: You built this practice from nothing. The picture your in-laws hold of you does not erase that. Let your work remain your own path, done imperfectly but truly. Let that be your answer.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She does not coddle him. She tells him that self-contempt is a poison that stops all good from growing. She says to set his mind on something truly good and to stop fearing. The point is that past failure does not define you, and those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less; what they see is a role, and you were never only a role.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: Rules of conduct for a renunciant.
verse.sanskrit: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥
verse.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
verse.translation: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
verse.meaning: A teacher is laying down the ground rules for a renunciant. They are not telling them to seek out pleasure or run from pain. They are saying do not exhaust yourself chasing what feels good or avoiding what feels bad. If someone praises you, do not swell with pride. If someone blames you, do not curse them in return. The lesson is to steady your mind and keep your energy for what is real, not to waste it on the swings of approval and blame.
verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.for_you: When your in-laws speak of your future as if it is already written, speak from the calm center of what you actually built. State the facts about your practice in a steady, even tone. Let them hear the truth of your work, not the picture they are trying to draw over it.

verse.speaker: Brihaspati (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Brihaspati counsels Indra on how to hold authority among difficult people.
verse.sanskrit: मृदुमप्यवमन्यन्ते तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः / मातीक्ष्णो मा मृदुर्भूस्त्वं तीक्ष्णो भव मृदुर्भव
verse.line: People walk over the soft and fear the harsh. Be firm when it's needed, gentle when it's needed.
verse.translation: People look down even on the gentle, and they shrink from the harsh. Do not be only harsh, do not be only soft: be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is.
verse.misuse: Firmness here means clarity, not cruelty.

matched.label: I have to give someone bad news

verse.meaning: Brihaspati tells Indra that people will always look down on the gentle and shrink from the harsh. He advises Indra not to be only harsh or only soft, but to be firm when firmness is needed and gentle when gentleness is needed. The point is that authority is not a single tone. It is the ability to shift between two modes, to know which one the moment requires without losing oneself in either extreme.
verse.for_you: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.

story.title: Ahalya: the long wait ends
story.story_hook: For years a stone lay in an abandoned hermitage, and only a sage knew it was a woman waiting.
story.summary: On the way to Janakpur, Vishvamitra shows Ram a stone in an empty hermitage: Gautam's wife Ahalya, bearing a curse in a body of stone, longing for the dust of his feet. At his touch she rises, stands before him with folded hands, unable to speak for love, tears streaming, and asks only that her mind may always drink at his feet.
story.lesson: However long you have been frozen, being seen can bring you back to life.

matched.label: Everything in my life is changing at once

story.hook_title: Ahalya lay as a stone for years, waiting for Ram's footsteps
story.teaser: Ahalya lay as a stone for years, waiting for Ram's footsteps
story.for_you: Ahalya spent years as a stone, unseen and frozen, until one person looked at her and brought her back. The life you are building cannot stay frozen because someone looks away. Let them see what is there.

script: They are erasing the life you built from nothing. You built a CA practice from zero. Now your in-laws speak of a future where you leave it, and your husband changes the subject. You feel yourself being erased, and your fury is quiet because you are standing alone.
Arjuna is on the battlefield, facing his own family. He is asking what is right. Krishna is answering him. Krishna says:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः.
In plain words: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.

This is about a borrowed life. It is about taking on a role that was never yours and trying to perform it perfectly. But a borrowed life is full of fear because you are always waiting to be found out. Your own path, with all its flaws and stumbles, is the only one that is truly yours. It is easier to walk your own road imperfectly than to walk someone else's perfectly.
You are not in their story. You are in yours. The practice you built from nothing is the truth of who you are. Let them speak of a future they have not lived. Your path is not borrowed. It is yours.
What is yours to own cannot be taken away.

depth.life: Your in-laws speak of a future you have not lived, and your husband changes the subject. You built your CA practice from nothing, and now they speak over it as if it were already decided.
depth.points: A borrowed life is dangerous. The duty that is yours alone, even imperfectly done, is better than another's done perfectly. Your practice is your own duty. No one else's. It cannot be taken by the picture they hold.
depth.practice: Look at the work you built from nothing and name one thing about it that is yours alone. Write it down.
depth.question: What part of your practice do you know is yours alone?
